subject: Sparse-route sampling and per-tenant drill controls
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Tempo AI ask — sampling + per-tenant drill controls

Forwarding the customer notes from Tempo (below). They want two things: (1) the Console to let them configure sampling at the "route" level (not just global sampling) so they can selectively sample high-cardinality tenants and (2) a quick drill UI to show sampled traces/requests for a given tenant/route (time-range + token-level cost breakdown).

Key context from the call: Tempo has a small number of routes that account for 75% of token spend. They need: sampling that can be set per-route and per-tenant (e.g., 1% for high-volume tenant A, 100% for tenant B during incident), the Console UI to expose a sampled request viewer with token/cost breakdown (unblended tokens per model variant), and a way to attach a short retention window for sampled records (48 hrs default).

They also attached a CSV of sample request IDs and time slices (attached: tempo_usage_sample.csv) and asked for a quick mock of the UI — they sent a doc which I converted to a PDF mock (console_sparse_route_mockups_v2.pdf).

Customer asks for an estimate and whether we can provide a short-term workaround (until UI ships) — e.g., admin API to set per-route sampling + an ad-hoc sampled-request export.

Please reply with feasibility notes and a rough timeline. We should flag any compliance/data-retention concerns (tempo is EU-based).

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Console ask: route sampling + per-tenant drill
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hey Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo. Quick recap from our side and a prioritized wishlist: 
- Per-route sampling controls (we want to limit sampling cost for noisy routes but keep 100% for critical routes)
- Per-tenant overrides (we run multi-tenant workloads; being able to pin tenants to higher sampling during incidents is critical)
- A lightweight viewer in Console to inspect sampled requests: timestamp, model variant, tokens (prompt/response), inferred cost per-request, and an easy export.
- TTL on sampled payloads (we prefer 48-72 hrs retention for sampled request bodies).

We attached a CSV of representative request ids and volumes. Any short-term way to do this via API would be great — otherwise we need to know roadmap timing.

—Emily

Attachments: tempo_usage_sample.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tempo AI ask — sampling + per-tenant drill

Thanks for the context, Marissa — good notes. High-level reactions from Product:

1) Per-route sampling surface: straightforward in principle (sampling key and rate per route id). Complexity grows if we support multi-dimensional overrides (route + tenant + model variant).
2) Sampled-request viewer: this touches our storage/retention model and the Console UX. We need to decide whether sampled payloads are stored in S3 with TTL or in an internal hot store. Retention + EU residency implications matter for Tempo.
3) Unblended token/cost breakdown by request: doable if we store model variant and token counts at ingest time; that data is already generated by the runtime but we don't persist it per-request today (only aggregate).

Quick questions for scope: (a) Does Tempo require per-tenant sampling rules that coexist with per-route rules? (b) Are they OK with sampled payloads being redacted for PII and stored for 48 hrs? (c) What scale are we talking about (sampled QPS) — CSV gives a hint but need a rough expected daily sampled requests number so we can size storage.

From a roadmap perspective:
- Short-term (2–3 weeks): admin API to set per-route sampling rate + ephemeral job for sampled-request export (engine side) — minimal Console changes (link to export task).
- Medium (8–12 weeks): Console UI for per-route/per-tenant sampling controls + sampled-request viewer with basic filters (time range, tenant id).
- Long-term (quart-er): integration with cost explorer to show unblended cost per sample and per-route heatmap.

I'll defer to Hannah for engineering constraints and Markus for SRE/cost implications. Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer | Product Manager, Observability | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tempo AI ask — sampling + per-tenant drill

Answers inline: 
(a) Yes — they want both. Default rule at route-level, with tenant-level overrides. Example: route /embed/bulk -> default 0.5% sampling, tenant A override 25% for incident window.
(b) They explicitly requested 48 hrs retention and are OK with automatic redaction of prompt text that matches a PII pattern. They asked for EU residency for the sampled payloads.
(c) CSV corresponds to ~1.2M requests/day across their account; they expect to sample ~0.1–0.5% initially (1.2–6k sampled requests/day).

They also asked about a temporary admin path we could call to run an export of sampled requests for a time range (we could charge for these exports).

Attaching customer CSV and the mock UI I sketched.

Marissa

Attachments: tempo_usage_sample.csv, console_sparse_route_mockups_v2.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tempo AI ask — sampling + per-tenant drill

Thanks for the detailed numbers — that makes sizing real. Engineering take:

- Short-term feasibility (admin API + export): HIGH. We already tag requests with route_id, tenant_id, model_variant and token counts at ingest. If we persist a small pointer (request_id, route_id, tenant_id, model_variant, token_counts, minimal metadata) into an S3-backed table keyed by day we can produce exports. We'll need to add a redaction step for prompt text and an EU-region write path. Approx effort: 2 engineer-weeks for API + export job + migration for EU writes.

- Medium-term (Console UI + per-route/per-tenant editing): MEDIUM. UI and RBAC for edits + validation, plus backend rule engine (matchers + precedence). Effort: 3–4 engineer-weeks across UI/backend.

- Storage/cost: At 6k sampled req/day and a 48-hr TTL, ~12k records live. With minimal JSON per sample (~1KB after redaction), cost is modest (~12MB/day), but request extraction jobs and searchability will bump costs if we enable text search. SRE should weigh in on index choices.

Open engineering questions:
- Do we want sampling rules to be evaluated at the edge (faster, lower write rate to core) vs evaluated centrally (simpler deployment)? Edge eval reduces writes but increases rollout complexity.
- How strict is EU residency? Do we need dedicated EU buckets for sampled payloads and separate keys?

I'll prototype the admin API and a one-click export that generates a CSV of sampled records for a time range.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
